items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: But that’s how he would start the concert. And I just thought well that’s historically valuable... But I talked to Mr. Hammond about this at one time... So I knew Mr. Hammond, I knew the music, and I was confident I could do it.

ctx.x: That’s some nice behind-the-scenes info right there. So I’ve got three or four things I’d like to get through today. And before the cameras were rolling you actually answered one of my questions. And it was about the “Spirituals to Swing” re-issue. And I was wondering, this might sound snarky, but what made you think — my question was, what made you believe you are qualified to take on that project. But then you answered me with all the photographs you were talking about.

Well I’ll tell you how that all came about. I was with Columbia Records for ten, eleven, twelve years. VP of A&R. And then that was when CBS, Columbia and Epic, and I think it was around 1989 Sony bought Columbia and Epic from CBS. And I stayed on. And then — I can’t remember exactly the year, I want to say ’97, ’96, ’95, ’96, Sony approached Dolly about doing her own imprint (this will lead to “Spirituals to Swing” believe it or not), her own imprint label. And she called it Blue Eye Records. So the records from…

great artist, no matter what, even the political backlash in the 50s, it was Vanguard. I said I’d do the same thing the Solomon Brothers do. Just find great artists no matter what the genre and make it an artist-friendly label. And he called me and he called me and picked my brain. And I remember getting off the phone one day and I remember telling my assistant then, Jenny, I said, “I think he’s going to offer me a job.” And she said, “What would you do?” I said, “I would take it and you would do it with me.…
